function: Multi-agent DQN selects the beam-hopping pattern (cells illuminated by each satellite beam per time slot) in a multi-satellite LEO downlink (pp. 1, 6-7).
system: Downlink from 16 LEO satellites at 1000 km, 8 beams and 37 cells per satellite, Ka-band 20 GHz, ten 10 MHz segments; no RIS (pp. 11-13).
method: Multi-agent double DQN, one agent per satellite with shared parameters, six fully connected layers; reinforcement learning on queue states, reward combining throughput and latency (pp. 6-7, 11).
data_channel: Custom LEO simulator (Table I): altitude 1000 km, 20 GHz, antenna gains; channel-gain model not specified; Poisson arrivals, 35-105 Mbps per cell random walk (pp. 4, 11).
test_conditions: Training shown at beta 0.7, 35 Gbps (Fig. 3); results averaged over 2,000 time slots across traffic, beta and satellite-count sweeps; no unseen-condition test stated (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Non-learned: greedy original benchmark, pre-scheduling BH plan [14], maximum USWG [21], variants without resource allocation or load balancing; learned: multi-agent DRL with adjacent beam avoidance [26] (pp. 12-13).
metrics: Throughput per cell, latency metric (delay fairness plus maximum queuing delay), average reward, and iterations to converge (pp. 5, 11-14).
complexity: Complexity orders only, no runtime: DQN proportional to its parameter count (p. 7), MM resource allocation (p. 9), load balancing (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 11: "the transmission frequency is set to the Ka-band at 20 GHz, while a circular antenna with an aperture radius of 0.1 m is utilized"; p. 3 only says the channel gain "is defined as" h. Custom simulator: no 3GPP TR 38.811 model, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "and the total data rate of input traffic is 35 Gbps" (training reward, Fig. 3); pp. 12-14 sweep traffic rate, trade-off coefficient and satellite count (p. 14: "Each satellite independently determines the BH pattern by DQN"), but the paper never states that the trained DQN is applied to conditions unseen in training instead of retrained.
q3_support: p. 12: "the proposed method is compared with the multi-satellite DRL approach presented in [26]" (learned); non-learned: "maximum USWG method [21] is evaluated" and "the pre-scheduling BH time plan method [14] is also compared"; compared on throughput and latency in Fig. 5.
q4_support: p. 7: "the computational complexity of Algorithm 2, which is proportional" to the number of DQN parameters; p. 9: "the overall computational complexity of Algorithm 3 is" given as an order in the system size and accuracy.
q5_support: p. 11: "The parameters utilized in the simulation are presented in Table I"; own simulator, no code or data link, no public dataset or measured data.
notes: Included as area 6: the learned part is the multi-agent DQN that picks each LEO satellite's beam-hopping pattern (beam control); power and frequency allocation (MM algorithm) and ISL load balancing are non-learned optimisation. Scheduling uses queue states and a latency term in the reward, so above_phy was weighed, but the DQN action is beam illumination, which the protocol counts as physical layer for satellite links. Tables I and II read on the page 11 image. q3 rests on the learned multi-agent DRL of [26]. Fig. 8 varies the number of satellites, but it is not stated whether the DQN is retrained, so q2 is 0.
